claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 typically has a hierarchical heterostructure in the as-cast or conventionally processed state.
A physics-informed machine-learning model can directly incorporate spatial maps of nanoprecipitates, phase boundaries, and local chemical ordering.
Spatial distributions of nanoprecipitates, phase boundaries, and local chemical ordering mediate stress transfer in HfNbTiVAl10.
Spatial distributions of nanoprecipitates, phase boundaries, and local chemical ordering mediate crack initiation in HfNbTiVAl10.
Embedding detailed microstructural descriptors enables the model to capture stress concentrations at heterointerfaces and early crack nucleation.
Standard finite-element and atomistic simulations typically miss these heterointerface and crack-nucleation interactions.
The proposed model will improve prediction of Young's modulus relative to established simulations.
The proposed model will improve prediction of yield strength relative to established simulations.
The proposed model will improve prediction of fracture behavior relative to established simulations.
The model will reduce RMSE for yield-strength and elastic-modulus predictions by approximately 20–30% relative to conventional simulation benchmarks.
The model will reduce computation time by at least one order of magnitude relative to traditional simulations.
The model will accurately capture coupled elastic-plastic-fracture behavior.
Full-scale finite-element and atomistic simulations generally have higher computational costs than the proposed surrogate model.
Conventional simulations have larger error margins for HfNbTiVAl10 mechanical-property predictions when hierarchical microstructural features are not represented.
Predictive gains may diminish when microstructures differ substantially from the training data because of extreme heterogeneity, phase transformations, or processing variations.
Machine-learning studies on other high-entropy alloys provide preliminary support for predicting mechanical properties with ML.
The exact error reduction and speedup for HfNbTiVAl10 remain uncertain pending representative training data and independent validation.
The intended application domain is room-temperature, quasi-static tensile and fracture loading involving elastic and plastic deformation.
A deviation greater than 20% between model predictions and independently measured key mechanical properties is declared falsifying.
Failure to achieve at least a tenfold computation-time reduction relative to traditional simulations is declared falsifying.
